rules.title: The market's overround is computed and recorded
rules.description: Every decision records the full market and the overround derived from it: the sum of the implied probabilities, minus one.
rules.rationale: The margin is the house's edge and the bettor's first cost. A decision that never computes it is a decision that never priced its own transaction costs.
rules.remediation: Record every outcome in the market with its price, and compute the overround from them.
rules.$assuranceNote: Full assurance over the recorded market. A market recorded with outcomes missing would produce a smaller overround and this check cannot tell the difference — which is why the schema requires the complete market rather than trusting it.

rules.title: The vig removal method is declared
rules.description: Every decision names the method used to convert implied probabilities into fair probabilities.
rules.rationale: Different methods give different fair probabilities and therefore different edges. A fair probability without a named method cannot be reproduced, and cannot be compared with one computed another way.
rules.remediation: Record the vig removal method used. This pack supports the multiplicative (proportional) method.
rules.$assuranceNote: Full assurance that a supported method is named and that the recorded fair probabilities follow from it.

rules.title: Vig is never ignored
rules.description: No edge or expected value is derived from raw implied probabilities. The bookmaker's margin is removed first, from the full market, by a declared method.
rules.rationale: Comparing an estimate against the raw implied probability treats the house margin as though it were free. On a standard two-way market that is roughly a two-and-a-half point head start handed to the book on every wager, and it is large enough to turn a losing process into one that looks profitable on paper.
rules.remediation: Remove the vig from the full market before computing edge, and recompute every downstream value.
rules.$assuranceNote: Detects a fair probability that was not derived from the recorded market, including the specific case where it equals the raw implied probability. It cannot detect a market recorded incompletely, which would understate the margin while passing every check here.
